notes:
Background: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics/workflow) embedding conversational support + search. Started on Redwood hosted API for fast integration; POC showed improved latency and lower token cost compared to incumbent. Team now wants Dedicated for predictable unit economics and VPC isolation.

POC highlights / asks:
- Workload: primarily support-agent chat + doc search + occasional reranking for candidate ranking.
- Targets: p95 latency <= 250ms for chat (512 tokens), throughput to support ~200 concurrent agents during peak, ~30M tokens/month initial target.
- Cost sensitivity: finance wants committed ARR in $150k-$300k range; prefers predictable monthly commits over heavy overages.
- Model prefs: open model family (Redwood-verified variants) with ability to fallback to smaller quantized variant during bursts.

Commercial ask (current negotiation):
- Commit level: proposing 12-month reserved capacity; initial commit = equivalent of 4 A100-type GPU-pools (baseline) for months 1-3 ramp to 8 pools by month 6. Asking Redwood for month-1 ramp credits (50%) to hit product launch.
- Burst: need burst to 2x baseline for seasonal spikes (marketing campaigns). Request documented burst policy (minutes/hour limits) and priority routing.
- Overage: counter-offer requested: overage at 1.25x unit rate if sustained > 14 days; immediate bursts billed at 1.5x but capped monthly. Finance dislikes open-ended 2x overage pricing.
- Cancellation / break clause: 90-day notice after month 6; service credits for missed latency SLOs.
- Ramp schedule: explicit month-by-month GPU pool targets in contract; option to increase commit at pre-negotiated unit price steps.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO (SAML), KMS for keys, audit logging and monthly access reports.
- Data residency: product-data must remain in us-east-1 for now; legal wants explicit residency clause in Private control plane options if later moved on-prem.

Stakeholders & quotes:
- CTO (Alyssa Grant): "We need predictable unit economics before we bake this into pricing; overages kill gross margins."
- Head of Product (Marco Ruiz): "Latency wins for end-user satisfaction — can tolerate a bit more cost but not unpredictable bills."
- Finance (Dirk Mason): pushing for step-down pricing for committed 12-month contract.

Open items for AE/SE follow-up:
- Provide formal term sheet with: committed GPU-hours equivalents, burst policy (hard caps), detailed overage formula, and ramp credits.
- Confirm reserved capacity billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and early-exit penalties.
- Supply SOC2 attestation + infra architecture note for VPC deployment. Link to security FAQ provided.
- Legal to review residency clause and indemnity language.

Next meeting: commercial deep-dive w/ pricing engineer + finance (week of 2026-03-08).
